sentence: That invariance is specific to the compound tense; the moment the same participle stands alone as an adjective (*la carta escrita*), it starts agreeing again, whereas [French](/french-past-participle/) has its own agreement rules for participles with avoir, with être and as adjectives.
note: Entire current French participle target body and ALL FAQ actually read this round. Target distinguishes avoir preceding-direct-object agreement, être subject agreement with pronominal qualifications, and adjectival agreement. No Spanish-style blanket invariance asserted for French.
target_quote: 'Pronominal verbs also use être, but agreement depends on their type. Essentially pronominal verbs such as se souvenir generally agree with their subject. S\'arroger is an exception: its participle agrees with a preceding direct object. Occasionally pronominal uses such as se laver or se parler instead require the direct-object test, including whether se is direct or indirect and whether a separate direct object precedes the verb. That mechanism, including why it produces agreement in some pronominal sentences and not others, is covered in full in [the French reflexive verbs guide](/french-reflexive-verbs/); the guide distinguishes subject agreement from the direct-object test, rather than applying one rule to every pronominal verb.',
